text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro met prime Minister Romano Prodi and another six ministers in the majority coalition to discuss ways to tackle Italy's mounting unemployment problem quickly. Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani illustrated a plan to promote investments for 10 trillion lire in the "depressed areas" of the poor south and create 150,000 new jobs in two years (all).
* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Brtinotti was reportedly satisfied with his meeting with Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) head Massimo D'Alema (all).

* Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi met German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and reportedly told him he intends to back the government's mini-budget in order to help Italy meet the EMU target. According to Berlusconi, Kohl is worried about the role of Bertinotti inside the majority coalition (all).
* The EEC decided to cut Italy's agriculture funds by 320 billion lire after Italian farmers refused to pay EU-imposed fines for surplus milk production (all).

* Talks between state telecommunication holding Stet and US giant At&t are reportedly holding talks to join their businesses in Latin America. The two companies intend to participate in the bid for the sell-off of Brasil's telephone company Telebras. Shares in state telecommunication holding Stet rose 2.8 percent on the Milan stock exchange, although both companies declined to comment (Sole 24 Ore).

*Italian investment funds had a net inflow of 14.920 trillion lire in February, slightly down on a historic high net inflow of 18.327 trillion lire in January. Equity funds saw a rise in net inflow to 2.345 trillion lire from 1.795 trillion lire in January (all).
* An internal study of the International Monetary Fund said a minibudget of 20 trillion lire will be necessary if Italy wants to bring its deficit/GDP ratio down to three percent (La Repubblica).

* Maurizio Romiti, son of Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti, will be named managing director of industrial holding HPI, just spun off from financial holding Gemina. HPI will be quoted on the Milan bourse from Monday (La Repubblica).
* Industrial turnover rose 0.6 percent year-on-year in December while orders fell 5.9 percent (all).

* Giorgio Fossa, chairman of industrialists' association Confindustria, after defining Italian industries outlook as at least stagnant, said that it is only by applying labour flexibility that the unemployment problem can be resolved (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
